nodes.label: Participation Score
nodes.rationale: Balances rewards for frontier breadth and fresh activation against penalties for regional concentration and repeated same-family streaks.

nodes.label: Narrow Oscillation
nodes.rationale: Repeatedly reuses limited move sources and localized board zones, creating potential stagnation and limited frontier expansion.

nodes.label: Broad Participation
nodes.rationale: Distributes activity across varied piece types and board quadrants to support expansive search, frontier growth, and fresh activations.

nodes.label: Rewards
nodes.rationale: Positive score terms encourage frontier width and fresh activation.

nodes.label: Penalties
nodes.rationale: Negative score terms suppress hot-region concentration and same-family streaks.

nodes.label: Tactical Move Clamping
nodes.rationale: Clamps the penalty so it cannot overwhelm a forcing line.

nodes.label: Fast local snapshot
nodes.rationale: Provides rapid startup using only a compact recent history.

nodes.label: Full archive recovery
nodes.rationale: Restores the complete data history asynchronously after the fast boot path.

nodes.label: hydrating
nodes.rationale: Restores application state from persistence during the hydration phase.

nodes.label: Stale archive dropped
nodes.rationale: Prevents a stale archive from overwriting live state that the user has already mutated.

nodes.label: Quiescence Tactical Extension
nodes.rationale: Extends analysis beyond the arbitrary maxDepth cutoff to continue evaluating tactical positions.

nodes.label: Safe Immutable API
nodes.rationale: The diagram labels this API as safe because it updates the board immutably while preserving untouched-cell identity.

nodes.label: Structural Sharing
nodes.rationale: Untouched cells preserve identity between the previous and next board, reducing allocation.

nodes.label: Search-Friendly Allocation Cost
nodes.rationale: The diagram associates identity-preserving updates with search-friendly allocation cost.

nodes.label: Naive Deep Clone
nodes.rationale: The diagram presents naive deep cloning as the rejected alternative to immutable structural sharing.

nodes.label: Canonical turnLog
nodes.rationale: The turnLog is shared once; undo and redo frames act as cursors rather than duplicated histories.

nodes.label: Lightweight cursors
nodes.rationale: UndoFrames are lightweight cursors and do not duplicate the histories represented by the shared turnLog.

nodes.label: Negamax Transformation
nodes.rationale: The parent score is computed as the negation of the child score when changing perspective between alternating players.
